skill.name: autonomous-agents
skill.description: Design reliable autonomous AI agents with constrained autonomy, agent loop patterns, goal decomposition, guardrails, and production reliability practices.
skill.summary: Guides reliable autonomous agent design through constrained loops, guardrails, validation, and failure-aware planning.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown inline backticks around related skill names in SKILL.md. No executable code, shell command guidance, data exfiltration intent, or prompt injection language was found in the audited file.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 68 uses Markdown backticks to format related skill names, not shell execution syntax. The skill is prompt-only and contains no executable code or command invocation path.

content.value_statement: Autonomous agents can fail as small step errors compound. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design constrained loops with guardrails.
actual_capabilities: Explains ReAct, Plan-Execute, and reflection patterns for agent loops.
Guides goal decomposition for constrained autonomous workflows.
Highlights guardrails, structured logging, cost limits, and least privilege.
Identifies anti-patterns such as unbounded autonomy and trusting agent outputs.
Encourages validation against ground truth before production use.
limitations: Provides design guidance, not a ready-to-run agent framework.
Does not include executable code, scripts, or external tool integrations.
Does not guarantee agent reliability without testing and monitoring.
Requires users to provide domain goals, tools, and safety constraints.

use_cases.title: Plan a Safe Agent Workflow
use_cases.description: Turn a broad automation goal into bounded steps, checks, and stop conditions.

use_cases.title: Review an Agent Architecture
use_cases.description: Assess loops, tools, guardrails, and logging before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Improve Production Reliability
use_cases.description: Find failure points caused by compounding errors, weak validation, or excess autonomy.

prompt_templates.title: Define the Agent Goal
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define a narrow autonomous agent goal. Identify allowed actions, required inputs, success criteria, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Agent Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare ReAct, Plan-Execute, and reflection patterns for my agent idea. Recommend the safest loop and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Add Guardrails
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned agent workflow. Add guardrails for cost limits, tool permissions, validation, logging, and human approval.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this autonomous agent design for production readiness. Focus on compounding error risk, recovery paths, monitoring, and least privilege.

output_examples.input: A team wants an agent to triage support tickets and draft replies.
output_examples.output: A bounded Plan-Execute workflow with ticket classification, evidence checks, draft generation, confidence scoring, and human approval for risky replies.

output_examples.input: A developer asks why a multi-step research agent fails after several actions.
output_examples.output: A reliability review showing compounding step errors, missing ground truth checks, weak logging, and a shorter loop with validation after each action.

output_examples.input: A manager wants to automate account changes without review.
output_examples.output: A safer design that limits autonomy, requires least-privilege tools, logs each action, and pauses for approval before account updates.

best_practices: Start with narrow tasks and add autonomy only after reliability is proven.
Use guardrails, cost limits, validation, and structured logging from the first design.
Test against ground truth and measure failure rates across full multi-step runs.
anti_patterns: Giving an agent unbounded autonomy before observing real failure modes.
Trusting agent outputs without validation or confidence checks.
Building a general-purpose agent when a constrained workflow would be safer.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design autonomous agent workflows that use bounded loops, guardrails, validation, and monitoring.

faq.question: Does it include executable agent code?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture and reliability guidance for use with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Which agent patterns does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers ReAct loops, Plan-Execute workflows, reflection patterns, goal decomposition, and self-correction.

faq.question: How does it reduce production risk?
faq.answer: It emphasizes narrow scope, hard limits, least privilege, structured logging, and validation against known outcomes.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is useful for product managers, engineers, and reliability teams planning AI agent systems.

faq.question: Can it evaluate an existing design?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review agent loops, failure points, tool permissions, monitoring, and readiness for production use.
